title: Flow Control Power Comparator
description: Prediction-challenge line chart: the learner ranks an outlet damper, variable inlet vanes and speed control by illustrative shaft power at 80%, 70% and 50% airflow and types the best method's saving, then sees the curves, a first-attempt score and mastery line, and an airflow selector that reports the powers and savings at any 5% step.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: flow control
outlet damper
variable inlet vanes
speed control
fan laws
brake horsepower

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Flow control methods and fan shaft power
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate outlet dampers, variable inlet vanes and speed control by the shaft power each needs at reduced airflow, correctly ranking the three methods and estimating the savings gap at a stated airflow between 50% and 100% of design.

accessibility.notes: Chart canvas has role=img and an aria-label; verdicts and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); feedback uses ✓/✗ glyphs with solid/dashed borders; series differ by colour, dash pattern and point shape, and marker value labels name the method in dark text; native selects, text input, buttons and range slider; Enter checks, Enter again goes to the next challenge, arrow keys move the airflow selector.

controls.label: Lowest / Middle / Highest
controls.purpose: Rank the three methods from lowest to highest shaft power

controls.label: Best method's saving vs. damper
controls.purpose: Type the saving in percentage points

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset every challenge and the score

controls.label: Airflow selector
controls.purpose: Explore mode: 50-100% airflow in 5% steps, default 70%; shows the three powers and two savings

equations: Saving = damper power − method power (percentage points)
rules: Damper and inlet-vane values between table rows by straight-line interpolation
A challenge is correct when the ranking is speed control, inlet vanes, outlet damper and the saving is within ±3 percentage points
Two attempts per challenge; after the second wrong attempt the answer is shown and the challenge counts as missed
assumptions: System curve through zero, so the speed ratio equals the airflow ratio
limitations: Real speed control has small drive losses
A system with fixed static pressure saves less than the ideal cube value

sources: Speed-control values: ideal fan-law cube relation (FP.models.fanLawRatios)
Outlet damper and inlet vane values: illustrative values written for Chapter 18, not Twin City Fan test data
Ordering supported by FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 145, 182, 183, 188

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal challenges followed by guided exploration
keyQuestions: At 80% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
At 70% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
At 50% airflow, which method uses the least power, and how much does it save compared with an outlet damper?
commonMisconceptions: Closing a damper to half flow cuts power roughly in half.
All flow-control methods save about the same energy.
Inlet vanes save as much as speed control.
Power falls in proportion to airflow when speed is reduced, rather than with roughly the cube of the airflow.
assessmentOpportunities: Running score 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 on the first attempt (80%, 70%, 50% airflow; ranking plus saving within ±3 percentage points; two attempts each).
